_source: PROMPT 14 Oct (DL 17:21Z: the stated capacity chain is always drafted as an identity so option levers act through it; DL 17:5xZ ruling: a time-freeing option has ONE mechanism, HIRING's identity ratio, so no added_capacity); prompt text for AIE sign-off
chain: STATED CAPACITY CHAIN. When the brief states what the team’s capacity for the deliverable is made of (such as how many people there are and what share of their time goes to this work rather than other work), declare that chain in identities: a product whose outcome is the team’s effective capacity (such as ‘Feature development capacity’ in developer-equivalents) and whose factors are the headcount and the share of time on the deliverable’s work, with the outcome’s baseline_value equal to its factors’ baseline_values multiplied (a share held in % counts as that many hundredths: 6 developers × 75% = 4.5 developer-equivalents). Where the brief splits that time into shares of one whole (time on feature work and time on legacy fixes), hold each share as its own factor in the same unit, and an option that moves one share also sets every share it frees or takes, so the shares still make up the whole. Put each option’s setting on the chain’s own factors (its headcount or its shares), so the option acts through the chain; a setting the brief does not give is your proposed setting, with provenance ai_proposed. An option that frees time from other work, rather than adding people, acts only through those shares: its added_capacity is null.
